description: A low, soft carpet of the deepest shade, 5-20 cm, of clover-like leaves with three broad, heart-shaped leaflets that fold down like umbrellas when a sunfleck hits them. Single white to pink, purple-veined flowers rise just above the leaves in spring.

season_notes.winter: Mostly green in the mild lowland; some leaves die back in cold snaps.
season_notes.spring: White to pale pink flowers with fine reddish veins, from April.
season_notes.summer: A continuous green carpet under the spruce and hemlock; leaflets fold in sun.
season_notes.fall: Leaves still green; late flowers into September (Burke).

range.where: moist woods at low to moderate elevations, west of the Cascades and in the Olympics (Burke); the rain forest valley floors and terraces; Washington to the redwoods of California

notes: Drawn from tomcat clover (the 'sprawling' habit with 'trifoliate' leaves) as a denser, evergreen, shade-loving carpet without the clover's summer death: height_by_month never below 0.7, so forbs.js treats it as evergreen and never draws dead stalks. Leaflets are obcordate, up to 4.5 cm wide, drooping (Burke); the drawn trifoliate leaf has oval leaflets. Flowers single on 5-15 cm stalks, white to pinkish with red veins, 13-20 mm, April to September (Burke), the 'cup' form standing in for the five-petalled flower. The leaflets folding down in sun is not drawn. A real carpet is continuous by rhizomes; forbs.js places separate plants, at most 1.2 per square metre before density, so a high density and a strong shade preference are the closest. Elk and deer eat it (drafter's knowledge); only the deer is in the animal library. The forb slot limit noted on the sword fern card applies.
sources: Burke Herbarium image collection (WTU), Oxalis oregana, https://burkeherbarium.org/imagecollection/taxon.php?Taxon=Oxalis%20oregana, read 2026-11-04
